key_insight: Reported gains in Multimodal Domain Generalization (MMDG) are often driven by inconsistent evaluation choices and narrow benchmarks; when evaluated under a unified, comprehensive protocol, many claimed improvements shrink or disappear.
problem_solved: Addresses fragmented, inconsistent evaluation practices and the lack of a broad, standardized benchmark for assessing true progress in MMDG across tasks, modalities, and domain shifts.
method: Assemble a comprehensive benchmark suite spanning multiple datasets, tasks (beyond action recognition), modality combinations, and realistic domain shifts.
Re-implement and evaluate representative MMDG algorithms under a single, standardized protocol (same splits, pretraining, metrics, and hyperparameter tuning) to enable fair comparison.
Perform systematic analyses to quantify how protocol differences, dataset selection, and modality choices affect reported performance and to produce best-practice recommendations.
impact: Provides a clear, reproducible foundation for comparing MMDG methods, helping researchers and practitioners distinguish genuine algorithmic advances from evaluation artifacts and guiding future robust multimodal model design.
visual_elements: Protocol flowchart: pipeline showing unified data splits, pretraining, tuning, and evaluation steps.
Before vs After bar chart: algorithm performance under original published protocols vs. unified benchmark (illustrates performance drops/shifts).
Dataset × Modality heatmap: coverage of datasets and modality combinations in prior work versus proposed benchmark.
Checklist/scorecard iconography: key recommendations for reproducible MMDG evaluation (e.g., common splits, reporting standards, modality ablations).
paper_title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study
paper_authors: Hao Dong, Hongzhao Li, Shupan Li, Muhammad Haris Khan, Eleni Chatzi
